best_use: Real-world cross-model sanity checks on derived TTC/jerk/deceleration distributions using the 100Hz (rlog) subset only; NOT suitable for fitting continuous brake-response transient shape because pedal signal is binary, not continuous.
limits: Naturalistic ADAS engagement/disengagement is not a controlled L3 TOR experiment; driver prior/familiarity not identified; brake input is binary; mixed sampling rate means any t_delay-relevant use must filter to the 100Hz subset explicitly or results will be a sampling-rate artifact, not a physical finding.

type: naturalistic EV kinematics (not a takeover dataset)

brake_accel_signal_type: CONFIRMED in Phase 0.3: state_gas_pos is a genuine CONTINUOUS accelerator-pedal field (26 distinct values, range 0.0-0.235 in sampled window). brake, brake_padel_status, act_ctrl_brake exist as fields but were CONSTANT/ZERO in both sampled windows of the one session inspected - NOT independently confirmed populated with a real braking event.
commanded_vs_actual: CONFIRMED in Phase 0.3: act_ctrl_gas/brake/accel and aTarget are continuous automation-COMMAND fields, populated only while op_enable=True (openpilot actively controlling) - both sampled windows had op_enable=False throughout, so these fields read constant 0, which is a real automation-authority artifact, not evidence the fields never populate.
ttc_derivable: Not applicable - not a hazard-approach dataset in the takeover sense
jerk_derivable: YES from continuous aEgo trace (confirmed populated with real variation in both windows)
vehicle_model_identity: YES - directory structure confirmed per-model (e.g. Hyundai_IONIQ_5) via GitHub Contents API
license: Still not confirmed to SPDX precision; repo states 'open-source license' only
access_method: CONFIRMED in Phase 0.3: real per-session data.csv files ARE committed directly to the GitHub repo (not externally hosted) - e.g. Hyundai_IONIQ_5/bdda168c0c35fad7/2024-06-05--16-17-00/data.csv, 88,616,080 bytes, fetched via HTTP Range requests, no gating.
best_use: Empirical bounds for regen/pedal-to-deceleration response shapes IF a session with an actual braking/regen event is located and inspected (not yet done - only one session, no braking event captured in the two windows sampled).
limits: NOT a takeover/TOR dataset. No pre-extracted event/episode index (unlike D005) - episode extraction must be built from scratch by scanning continuous signals (see response_episode_definition.md). Regen magnitude (1-4 m/s^2 / 0.1-0.3g per README) remains UNVERIFIED against raw files after a genuine attempt - two real windows of one session captured no regen event.
audit_status: USABLE_PARAMETER_SOURCE (raw file access confirmed; regen-event content still unverified - requires further session scanning)
